title: Signal pruning schedule and trace ownership charter
content:
PURPOSE:
This doc is an operational charter for pruning low-value signals, scheduling dashboard slimming, and clarifying trace sampling ownership for inference services. Goal: reduce dashboard noise and query-costs by ~30% over three quarters while keeping investigations fast and reproducible.

BACKGROUND / WHY NOW:
- We have ~250 widgets across tenant and runtime dashboards; many are stale or high-cardinality and cause expensive queries.
- Trace retention and sampling policies are inconsistent between hosted and private deployments, leading to unpredictable replayability.
- Observability engineers spend ~20% of oncall time tuning panels/queries.

DEFINITIONS (quick):
- Signal: any metric/trace/span/derived panel tile used on a dashboard or alert.
- Candidate-for-prune: <1% query hits in last 90 days OR >$0.10/query on average OR owner unresponsive after two review cycles.
- Trace anchor: minimal span set required to reconstruct a user-visible incident (request id, routing, model-call, kvcache events).

PRINCIPLES:
1) Preserve investigator flow: Every pruning decision must map to a reduced microdash showing the investigation path made from remaining tiles.
2) Cost-aware removal: Prefer query rewrite / pre-aggregation before deletion.
3) Ownership first: Each signal must have an owner or be marked as "orphan" and scheduled for deprecation.

SCHEDULE (quarterly cadence):
- Week 1: Signal census export (SQL + dashboard usage) + rough cost score.
- Week 2: Owner outreach + rewrite proposals for top 20 expensive queries.
- Week 3: Canary rewrite + query TTL experimentation (48–96h).
- Week 4: Prune window + archive notes to /confluence/obs/signal-archive.
Repeat quarterly.

HOW TO SCORE A SIGNAL (simple heuristic):
- UsageScore = log(1 + hits_last_90d) * 0.4
- CostScore = min(1, avg_query_cost_usd / 0.5) * 0.35
- InvestigationValue = has_trace_anchor ? 1 : 0.25
- Composite = UsageScore * 0.5 + CostScore * 0.35 + InvestigationValue * 0.15
- Candidate-for-prune if Composite < 0.2 and owner absent.

TRACE POLICY NOTES (owner: Evan Li):
- Sampling tiers: 100% capture for P0 tenant requests (customer-facing incidents), 10% for P1s, 1% for general background traffic (default).
- Retention tiers: hot traces (full spans) 7 days, warm traces (sparse spans) 30 days, cold traces (ids + minimal anchors) 90 days.
- For private deployments, default is 1% sampling unless customer opts-in for 100% (via support change request).
- Always capture trace anchors for any request that triggers an alert or rollback.

DASHBOARD PRUNING CHECKLIST (what to do before deleting a tile):
- [ ] Confirm query hit count < 1% over 90d OR cost > $0.10 avg
- [ ] Raise in team sync and ping owner (2 attempts)
- [ ] Attempt rewrite with pre-aggregation (materialized view / daily rollup)
- [ ] Run canary for at least 48h and validate no investigator pain points
- [ ] Archive query + reason + sample result to Confluence
- [ ] Remove tile and add deprecation note in dashboard footer for 7 days

EXAMPLE SQL SNIPPET (simple usage export):
-- run weekly export to get per-panel usage and avg query cost
SELECT panel_id, panel_title, COUNT(1) AS hits_last_90d, AVG(query_cost_usd) AS avg_cost
FROM observability.query_logs
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY panel_id, panel_title
ORDER BY hits_last_90d DESC;

QUICK COST FORECAST TEMPLATE (notes for finance):
- Baseline: current monthly query spend for dashboards = $X (query engine + storage amortized).
- Target: reduce hotspots by 30% in 3 quarters through pruning + rollups.
- Conservative projection: 15% first quarter, 25% second, 30% by end of third.
- Major levers: rollups (40% reduction on heavy panels), sampling (20% on traces), TTL reductions (10%).

OWNERSHIP CHARTER (roles):
- Signal steward: person responsible for the metric/span (owns outreach). Default: product-engineer owning the feature.
- Observability curator: person who runs quarterly census and enforces schedule (Priya Shah).
- Trace owner: person who defines trace anchor for a service (Evan Li).
- Dashboard maintainer: community member responsible for dashboard UX (rotating 3-month assignment).

ORPHAN HANDLING RULES:
- Signals with no owner after two outreach attempts -> flagged as ORPHAN and put on 60d deprecation timer.
- During 60d, curator tries to match to owning teams via code search, Alert/PR history, and customer hits.
- If unresolved, archive and remove after deprecation.

RISK & MITIGATION:
- Risk: Investigators lose necessary context after pruning.
  Mitigation: mandatory microdash to reconstruct incidents; roll back removal for 7 days if pager incidents increase.
- Risk: regressions in rollout due to missing traces.
  Mitigation: keep trace anchors for 90 days; increase sampling temporarily during rollouts.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (notes-to-self style):
- Which query engine metric do we use for exact cost attribution? (Prometheus push vs query-engine billing) (TODO Evan)
- Should we automate owner ping via Slack bot? (nice-to-have)
- Make a small "prune playbook" script that runs the checks and drafts Confluence archive entry.

RECENT ACTIONS / HISTORY:
- 2025-10: small pilot pruned 18 low-value tiles on ops dashboard — mean query latency dropped 22%, cost down 11% for that dashboard.
- 2025-11: trace anchor spec added for model-serving (svc-model) — initial owner: Jonah Reed.

APPENDIX (links and quick references):
- Archive: /confluence/obs/signal-archive (placeholder)
- Incident sample: jira/INC-1298 (shows why trace anchor mattered)
- Small rewrite PR: github.com/redwood/observability/pull/241

NOTES: keep this doc lightweight. We'll iterate after the first quarterly run.

---
Sign-off: Priya Shah (curator) | Evan Li (trace owner) | Marta Gomez (dashboard UX)
